---
title: "Week 12 Tutorial: Mixed-Effects Models I"
subtitle: "Wednesday tutorial · reinforces Monday's lecture on non-independence and random intercepts"
toc: true
---



## Goals

- Recognize non-independence from repeated measures or nested sampling
- Fit a random-intercept mixed model with `lme4`

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)  # adds p-values to lmer output
```
:::



## Why not just use `lm()`? Pseudoreplication revisited



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(21)
n_sites <- 8
n_per_site <- 6

field_data <- tibble(site = factor(rep(1:n_sites, each = n_per_site))) |>
  mutate(
    site_effect = rep(rnorm(n_sites, 0, 3), each = n_per_site),
    treatment = rep(rep(c("Control", "Treated"), n_per_site / 2), n_sites),
    response = 10 + ifelse(treatment == "Treated", 2, 0) +
      site_effect + rnorm(n(), 0, 1.5)
  )
```
:::



Measurements within the same site aren't independent — they share a
site effect. Ignoring that (treating all 48 rows as independent)
inflates your effective sample size and your false-positive rate.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_naive <- lm(response ~ treatment, data = field_data)
summary(m_naive)$coefficients
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
                  Estimate Std. Error   t value     Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)      10.863814  0.8896883 12.210810 4.910819e-16
treatmentTreated  2.117502  1.2582092  1.682949 9.916133e-02
```


:::
:::



## Random-intercept mixed model



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_mixed <- lmer(response ~ treatment + (1 | site), data = field_data)
summary(m_mixed)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}


:::



::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 1
Compare the standard error on the `treatment` coefficient between
`m_naive` and `m_mixed`. Which is larger, and why does that make
sense given that site is a real source of shared variation?
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(field_data, aes(treatment, response, color = site)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Response by treatment, colored by site](week12-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-sites-1.png){#fig-sites width=672}
:::
:::



::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 2
Refit `m_mixed` on a version of `field_data` with `n_sites <- 3`
instead of 8 (re-run the simulation with that change). Does the mixed
model still make sense with so few sites? (This is a preview of a
real limitation of mixed models — they need enough groups to estimate
the random-effect variance reliably, roughly 5–10 as a rule of thumb.)
:::
